blocks.text: Post-training quantization, PTQ, is the general category of quantizing a model after it has already finished training, covering everything from the simple, naive quantization approaches introduced earlier in this module to the more sophisticated GPTQ and AWQ algorithms, all sharing the property that they operate on an already trained model rather than requiring a training run of their own.

This closing topic of the Quantization module ties together everything covered across its earlier topics, framing GPTQ, AWQ, and simple uniform quantization all as different points within this same broader post-training category, contrasted directly against quantization aware training covered in the previous topic.
1. What Post-Training Quantization Means

blocks.alt: An already trained model gets quantized afterward, producing a deployed quantized model

blocks.text: Post-training quantization takes a model that has already completed its full training or fine-tuning process, covered throughout this course, and applies a quantization technique to it afterward, without needing to touch or rerun the original training process at all.
2. Quantizing After Training Completes

This ordering, train first, quantize second, is exactly what distinguishes post-training quantization from quantization aware training, covered in the previous topic, which builds quantization simulation directly into the training process itself rather than treating it as a separate, later step.
3. Post-Training Quantization vs QAT

blocks.alt: Post-training quantization takes minutes to hours while QAT requires a full training run

blocks.text: The fundamental tradeoff between the two approaches, covered directly in the previous QAT topic, comes down to speed versus quality, post-training quantization completes in minutes to hours since no training is involved, while QAT typically achieves somewhat better quality at aggressive precision levels but requires an entire training run.

blocks.text: 4. Calibration Data for Post-Training Quantization

blocks.alt: Representative sample data informs quantization choices

blocks.text: Like the specific techniques covered earlier in this module, post-training quantization in general benefits from calibration, a representative sample of data run through the model to inform quantization decisions, the same general concept introduced in the earlier What Is Quantization topic and applied specifically within GPTQ and AWQ.

blocks.text: 5. Speed and Simplicity Advantages

blocks.alt: No retraining needed means fast turnaround

blocks.text: The biggest practical advantage of post-training quantization is speed and simplicity, a team can take an existing fine-tuned model, covered throughout this course, and produce a quantized deployment version in a comparatively short amount of time, without needing to plan or budget for an additional training run.
6. Quality Tradeoffs of Post-Training Quantization

blocks.alt: A very aggressive target is compared against a moderate target

blocks.text: For moderate quantization targets, INT8 covered earlier in this module, for instance, post-training quantization typically preserves quality very well, but for more aggressive targets, 4-bit precision, the gap compared to quantization aware training becomes more noticeable, exactly the tradeoff explored in the previous QAT topic.
7. Where GPTQ and AWQ Fit In

blocks.alt: Simple uniform post-training quantization leads to smarter post-training quantization through GPTQ and AWQ

blocks.text: GPTQ and AWQ, covered in their own dedicated topics earlier in this module, are both sophisticated post-training quantization methods, they still fall within this same broad category, no retraining required, but use much smarter, calibration driven approaches than a simple, naive uniform quantization would, closing much of the quality gap against quantization aware training without paying its full training cost.

blocks.title: This topic is the unifying frame for the whole Quantization module
blocks.content: Every specific technique covered earlier in this module, INT8, INT4, GPTQ, AWQ, falls under this same post-training quantization umbrella, distinguished from quantization aware training by the simple fact that none of them require retraining the model.

blocks.text: 8. Post-Training Quantization for Fine-Tuned Models

Applying post-training quantization to a model that has already gone through the fine-tuning process, covered extensively throughout this course, SFT, LoRA, or full fine-tuning, is one of the most common practical workflows, letting a team produce an efficient deployment version without disturbing the fine-tuning work already completed.
9. When Post-Training Quantization Is Enough

For most deployment scenarios, post-training quantization, particularly using a smarter method like GPTQ or AWQ rather than naive uniform quantization, is sufficient, reserving quantization aware training specifically for the more demanding cases identified in the previous topic, where its extra cost is genuinely justified.
Worked Example

A team completes a fine-tuning process using LoRA, covered in the earlier module, and wants to deploy their finished model efficiently. Rather than incorporating quantization simulation back into a retraining run, they apply GPTQ as a post-training quantization step to their already merged, finished model, covered in the Merging Adapters topic.

The entire quantization process completes within a few hours, producing a deployment ready quantized model without needing to touch their original fine-tuning pipeline at all, exactly the speed and simplicity advantage post-training quantization offers over quantization aware training.
Common Mistakes

items: Applying naive uniform post-training quantization when GPTQ or AWQ, still fully post-training, would preserve meaningfully more quality
Reaching for quantization aware training by default without first trying whether post-training quantization alone is sufficient
Skipping calibration for post-training quantization when it would meaningfully improve the result
Not recognizing GPTQ and AWQ as specific instances of the broader post-training quantization category

For a fine-tuned model you have in mind, or one covered elsewhere in this course, sketch the post-training quantization workflow you would follow, from an already trained model through calibration and quantization to a deployment ready quantized version.
Key Takeaway

Post-training quantization covers the broad category of quantizing a model after training completes, without any retraining required, spanning everything from simple naive uniform quantization to the more sophisticated GPTQ and AWQ techniques covered earlier in this module, and it remains the practical default for most deployment scenarios given its speed and simplicity advantage over the more demanding quantization aware training approach.
